references.text: Jesus laid his hands on the sick and healed them. Laying on of hands as a healing method is a recurring feature in Jesus' ministry ([ref:Luk 4:40|Luke 4:40]).
Jesus promised that believers would lay hands on the sick, and they would be healed ([ref:Mark 16:18|Mark 16:18]).
Jesus laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them, just as he here laid his hands on the bent-over woman ([ref:Mark 6:5|Mark 6:5]).
Ananias laid his hands on Saul, and he regained his sight – laying on of hands as a means of healing in the early church ([ref:Apg 9:17|Acts 9:17]).
The blind man who was healed praised God – the same response as the healed woman in Luke 13:13, who also "glorified God" ([ref:Luk 18:43|Luke 18:43]).
The leper Samaritan returned and glorified God with a loud voice after being healed, a parallel example of praise following healing ([ref:Luk 17:15|Luke 17:15]).
The lame man at the Beautiful Gate was healed and entered the temple, "walking and leaping and praising God" – the same pattern of immediate healing and praise ([ref:Apg 3:8|Acts 3:8]).
The psalmist urges his soul to bless the Lord and not forget all His benefits, including that He heals all your diseases – a background for the woman's praise ([ref:Sal 103:1-2|Psalm 103:1-2]).
"The Lord lifts up those who are bowed down" – the woman who had been bent over for eighteen years was lifted up, a fulfillment of this promise ([ref:Sal 146:8|Psalm 146:8]).

Jesus himself explains the healing: this daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound for eighteen years, should she not be released from this bond? The context for the laying on of hands and the immediate healing ([ref:Luk 13:16|Luke 13:16]).
The expression "immediately" (παραχρῆμα) is also used of the lame man who stood up at once – the same Greek word for the immediate effect of Jesus' power ([ref:Luk 5:25|Luke 5:25]).
